baseline_prompt:
def is_sorted(lst):
    '''
    Given a list of numbers, return whether or not they are sorted
    in an order. If list has more than 1 duplicate of the same
    number, return False. Assume no negative numbers and only integers.
    '''

Clarification: Yes, up to 1 duplicate of the same number is allowed (a number may appear at most twice); more than 2 occurrences of the same value causes False.

Clarification: Allowed, True -- the False-triggering rule is specifically 'more than 1 duplicate of the SAME number' (i.e. one value appearing 3+ times), not multiple different values each appearing twice (confirmed by test case: [1,2,2,3,3,4] -> True).

candidates.question: Does the “more than 1 duplicate of the same number” rule apply to the total count of that number in the list (i.e., a value may appear at most twice) or to the number of duplicate *pairs* (i.e., at most one repeated value overall)?
candidates.answer: It refers to the TOTAL COUNT of that number anywhere in the list -- a value may appear at most twice; a third or later occurrence of the same value makes it False.
